examShortTricks: Trick 1: Art questions want the FUNCTION named: expression, communication, preservation of culture, therapy — pick two and argue, not a list.
Trick 2: When analysing a picture/poem in this unit, move from what you SEE to what it MEANS — observation then interpretation is the marking ladder.
Trick 3: 'Should art be censored?' type questions: state the principle (freedom of expression) then the limit (harm to others) — balanced principle-based answers win.
practiceQuestions: Q. Why is art important in society? Give two reasons. (2 marks) — expresses identity and preserves culture; provokes thought and change.
Q. Should all art be free from censorship? (2 marks) — defend expression, but accept limits where art incites harm.
keyPoints: Art reflects society — connect any artwork discussed to its social context.
Use sensory vocabulary (vivid, expressive, evocative) when describing art.
